title: Cushion rebound for a rolling, spinless ball
purpose: Validates the Han impulse model (doc section 5.1). The incidence angle is measured from the rail normal, so 0 deg is a square hit. The second block pins the vertical flip between the normal impulse (into the slate) and the friction impulse (upward), which is what produces the hop.

setup.note: the incoming velocity makes `incidence_angle` with the rail normal (+x); the ball is rolling, so omega = (k x v)/R

rail_regimes.case: lifted 20 mm (popped by a ball-ball collision)

measured_hop.notes: TO BE CALIBRATED: the hop height of a ball off the rail, measured from high-speed video, at a known nose height. The 3.8 mm the model predicts at the WPA spec height is a model output and not a measurement: it depends on treating the cushion impulse and the slate rebound as sequential, and Mathavan treats the table contact as simultaneous (doc section 5.1). Until this is measured, the hop numbers in the document are the model talking to itself.

invariants.statement: the rebound angle is identical for incident speeds of 1, 2 and 4 m/s at the same incidence angle (Mathavan Fig. 8)
the speed loss is largest for incidence angles around 40 deg (Mathavan, section 4)

the outgoing vertical velocity changes sign at eps_c/R = mu_cushion/sqrt(1 + mu_cushion^2) = 0.139 for mu_cushion = 0.14; above it the ball is pressed into the slate, below it the ball is launched upward. The WPA reference profile derives eps = 0.270 R and must therefore press the ball into the slate
the contact height comes from the specified nose height: eps = h_nose - R, so it is an output of the table spec rather than a tuned input
eps depends only on the nose height: the contact normal has no component along the rail, so a 40 degree approach gives the same eps and the same normal tilt as a square hit

the specified nose height is what sets the vertical impulse: at 0.500 D the cushion launches the ball upward (+0.49 m/s at 2 m/s) and at 0.635 D it presses the ball into the slate (-0.44 m/s). Reproducing both is the check that the contact height is the nose height

the solver must branch on the regime: nose rubber below h_nose, rail structure between h_nose and the rail top (~15 mm higher), and no contact above the rail top. The rubber model must not be extrapolated into the rail structure
